subject: Model recommendations + peak-hour token estimates for VeloxDocs onboarding
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@veloxdocs.com>, Samir Reddy <samir@veloxdocs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model recommendations + peak-hour token estimates for VeloxDocs onboarding

Hi Asha / Samir,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — helpful context. I did a quick pass with the modeling team and attached two artifacts: a compact shortlist (model_recs_shortlist.pdf) and the token estimates CSV (velox_token_estimates.csv). The short version of our recommendations:

- Tier A (default): redwood/gpt-medium-8k (INT8 quantized option) — good latency/cost balance for typical single-doc summarization and chat where average context is ~1.5–3k tokens.
- Tier B (long-running threads / deep context): redwood/gpt-large-32k — reserved for cases that exceed ~6k rolling context (e.g., multi-document review, entire conversation threads).
- Routing: default traffic to Tier A; route to Tier B when context_length_estimate > 6k tokens OR when request type == "document_batch".
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated document headers and user metadata (we expect ~20% token savings on repeat calls during sessions).
- Batching: suggest 40–80ms batching window for non-interactive batch jobs (ingest/summary jobs) and immediate pass-through for interactive chat.

Token estimates are conservative — the CSV contains hourly and peak-hour projections across three scenarios (Pilot, Ramp, Steady-state). A few numbers to call out for planning:
- Pilot (first 30 days): 120k tokens/day, peak hour ~12k tokens (~10% of daily).
- Ramp (months 1–3): 700k tokens/day, peak hour ~95k tokens (~13% of daily).
- Steady-state (post-month 3): 2.1M tokens/day, peak hour ~320k tokens (~15% of daily).

Questions for you: 1) Can you confirm the expected number of concurrent active users during your announced launch window (you mentioned a narrow beta with analytics team)? 2) Do you have any hard latency targets for UI flows (we want to ensure Tier A delivers p50/p95 within your SLA)?

Next steps: once you confirm those two items we’ll pull a quick cost/throughput sketch for each tier and propose a recommended Dedicated capacity profile you can review.

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@veloxdocs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Samir Reddy <samir@veloxdocs.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model recommendations + peak-hour token estimates for VeloxDocs onboarding

Thanks Soojin — this looks great and aligns with our internal thinking. Quick answers below and one small change request.

- Concurrent active users (beta): we expect ~85 concurrent active users during our 2-week beta (internal analytics + power users). For public launch in ~6 weeks we estimate up to ~1,200 concurrent active users at peak (concurrent = users with an open session and recent activity).
- Latency target: for the main editor flow we want p50 < 400ms and p95 < 1.2s for short-context requests (<= 3k tokens). For heavy batch document diffs we are fine with p95 < 2s.
- Change request: can you make the routing rule explicit for the "document_batch" path vs. chat so our engineers can mirror it in the proxy? e.g., route path /api/v1/doc-summarize -> Tier B when total_context_tokens > 6k; otherwise Tier A.

If these numbers look good to you, please send the cost sketch and a proposed date for the technical kickoff. We can provision a shared test S3 + sample dataset for load testing next week.

—
Asha Patel
Head of Product, VeloxDocs
asha.patel@veloxdocs.com

Subject: Internal: VeloxDocs routing/tier plan + ask list (cost, docs, throughput)

Team — looping you in to finalize our recommendation and split work. I captured Asha's replies above. Key design choices I want alignment on:

1) Model tiers and routing
  - Tier A: redwood/gpt-medium-8k (INT8) — default for interactive chat and single-doc summarization where context <= 6k tokens.
  - Tier B: redwood/gpt-large-32k — fallback for long-context cases and /api/v1/doc-summarize when total_context_tokens > 6k.
  - Fallback behavior: if Tier A is overloaded, we should auto-failover to a smaller-window response (trim context) and queue for Tier B, otherwise route to Tier B if capacity available.

2) Capacity/latency sizing assumptions (input from product):
  - Target p50/p95 for Tier A: 350ms / 1.0s (Asha wants p50 < 400ms).
  - Peak hour request profile: assume 15% of daily tokens fall in 1-2 peak hours. Use the Steady-state peak from CSV (~320k tokens/hour) as an upper bound.

3) Cost & Dedicated ask
  - Ben: can you run a quick per-hour and per-token cost sketch for the three scenarios in the CSV (Pilot, Ramp, Steady-state) including a Dedicated pool config (2x A100 equiv for Tier A, 3x A100 equiv for Tier B as starting point)?
  - Marissa: please prepare the CS handoff checklist and the brief for the technical kickoff (suggestion: 30-minute pre-kickoff tech alignment + 90-minute kickoff).
  - Karthik: confirm the stream/batch throughput knobs we'd recommend (batch window size, KV cache retention TTL, expected throughput/sec per GPU).

Asha/Samir — FYI we intend to send a cost sketch and a proposed Dedicated capacity plan tomorrow after Ben's numbers are in. Also planning to share a short runbook for handling long-context fallbacks during the first 2-week beta.

Ben Carter: "Will run numbers and attach a rough slide by EOD — will model 2x/3x/6x cluster sizes for sensitivity."
Marissa Cole: "I'll draft the handoff doc and a Kickoff agenda; aiming to have first draft in the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow."
Karthik Iyer: "I'll validate throughput assumptions with infra and confirm batching/TTL defaults by noon PT tomorrow."

Hi Asha / Samir — quick update and confirmed next steps now that we've internal alignment: 

- Model tiers & routing: same as discussed. Routing rule for your engineering team: route /api/v1/doc-summarize -> Tier B when total_context_tokens > 6000; otherwise Tier A. We'll provide a proxy snippet you can reuse.
- Capacity ask (sketch): Pilot: 1x A100 equiv (Tier A), Reserve cold Tier B capacity on demand. Ramp: 2x A100 equiv (Tier A) + 1x A100 equiv reserved for Tier B. Steady-state: 4x A100 equiv split across Tier A/B — Ben attached the cost sketch here: [attachment: velox_cost_sketch.pdf (PDF, 28KB)] and updated the Drive folder.
- Kickoff: Technical pre-alignment on May 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (30m); Full technical kickoff May 22, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT (90m). Please confirm availability.
- Load test: we'll coordinate S3 sample dataset and a short load plan (100k tokens/hour baseline, ramping to 350k tokens/hour peak).
- Docs & runbook: Marissa shared the CS handoff checklist and an ops runbook link in the Drive.

Action items for VeloxDocs:
- Confirm kickoff times (or propose alternatives).
- Share a small sample of anonymized documents for the load test (S3 link) and the expected traffic spike date if you have one.

Asha replied that the kickoff times look good and she'll share the S3 sample by Tuesday morning. We'll follow up with the DocuSign for the pilot Reserved capacity addendum after kickoff.
